text: Designing a good REST API is like building a clear road system for developers. First, your endpoints should be simple and logical, using nouns like `/users` or `/orders` instead of verbs. Always use proper HTTP status codes—for example, `201` when a resource is created, `404` when it is not found, and `500` for server errors. This helps clients understand what happened without reading the response body. Next, keep your documentation up to date with examples of requests and responses. Finally, never forget versioning. If you change your API later, keep the old version working by using URLs like `/v1/users`. These practices make your API reliable and easy to adopt.
